title: Outflowing shocked gas dominates the NIR H<SUB>2</SUB> emission from the dual AGN NGC 6240
question: To disentangle rotating and non-rotating (outflowing) molecular and ionised gas components in the central ~2 kpc of the dual AGN NGC 6240 and determine the origin and excitation mechanism of its bright NIR H2 emission.

data.arrays: 12m array (41 antennas in Band 7, 37 antennas in Band 3)
data.sensitivity: Band 7 continuum: 0.3 mJy/beam (1 sigma RMS); Band 3 line: 0.6 mJy/beam per 13 km s^-1 channel

what.value: VLBI positions of the two AGN

evidence.quote: The two AGN are marked using the Very-Long-Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) positions from (cite: Hagiwara+11).

what.value: ALMA Band 8 [CI](1-0) integrated outflow maps between (-650, -200) km s^-1 and (250, 800) km s^-1

evidence.quote: We use the same ALMA maps as shown in (cite: Cicone+18) (panels c and d of Figure 1 in that paper), which were obtained by integrating the \[CI\](1-0) line emission respectively between (-650, -200) km s$^{-1}$ (blue wing) and (250, 800) km s$^{-1}$ (red wing).
We use the E-MILES stellar population synthesis templates (cite: vazdekis_uv-extended_2016), which cover the wavelength range $0.168-5\,\mu$m at a spectral resolution of $2.51-23.57$ Å.

recipe.goal: Prepare and astrometrically align archival JWST NIRSpec IFU data cubes
recipe.method: Retrieve stage 3 NIRSpec IFU data cubes from MAST and apply astrometric offsets to align the 4.5 um continuum peak with the VLBI position of the S AGN, without performing wiggle corrections.
assumptions: The 4.5 um continuum peak coincides with the S AGN VLBI position

recipe.goal: Image ALMA Band 7 870 um continuum and Band 3 CO(1-0) line cube
recipe.method: Visually inspect Band 7 spectral windows to split out line-free channels and image with tclean (mfs); subtract continuum in Band 3 with uvcontsub (1st-order polynomial) and image CO(1-0) cube with tclean.
key_parameters: Band 7: specmode = mfs, hogbom, Briggs robust = 0.5, cell = 0.05'', mask radius = 1.3''
Band 3: specmode = cube, channel width re-binning = 5 (13 km s^-1), hogbom, Briggs robust = 0.5, cell = 0.08''

recipe.goal: Fit stellar continuum and derive stellar kinematics
recipe.method: Fit stellar continuum and absorption features spaxel-by-spaxel in the NIRSpec bands using pPXF with E-MILES templates, and visualize the orientation of the rotating stellar structures with kinemetry.
key_parameters: 1.0 um band: 5th-order additive and 2nd-order multiplicative Legendre polynomials; 1.7 um band: 5th-order additive and 3rd-order multiplicative Legendre polynomials; 2.9 um band: 6th-order additive and 3rd-order multiplicative polynomials
assumptions: Single kinematic stellar component per spaxel; VLBI positions of the two AGN selected as kinematic centres for kinemetry visualization.

recipe.goal: Decompose emission lines into rotating and non-rotating components and compute moment maps
recipe.method: Fit six NIR emission lines (Pa alpha, Pa beta, [FeII] 1.257 um, [FeII] 1.644 um, H2 1-0 S(1), H2 0-0 S(8)) spaxel-by-spaxel for spaxels with S/N > 10 using up to three Gaussians plus a linear baseline, tying one Gaussian to the pPXF stellar velocity and dispersion within 3 sigma, then compute 0th, 1st, and 2nd moment maps for total, rotating, and non-rotating components.
key_parameters: S/N > 10 cut; rotating component A in [0.1, 1.0] (init 0.3), mu_0 and sigma_lambda within 3 sigma of pPXF stellar values; non-rotating components A in [0.0, 1.0] (init 0.5 and 0.0), sigma_lambda in [0.0, 0.003] um (init 0.001 um)
assumptions: There is gas kinematically coupled with the stars sharing the same velocity and velocity dispersion as the stellar component in each spaxel.

recipe.goal: Fit PAH 3.3 um feature, compute H2/PAH and H2excitation ratios, and compare with ALMA cold gas and dust maps
recipe.method: Fit the PAH 3.3 um feature and blended H2 1-0 O(5) line at 3.235 um with two Gaussians, compute the H2 0-0 S(8)/PAH 3.3 um intensity ratio map and H2 2-1 S(1)/H2 1-0 S(1) line ratios, and compare morphologies and kinematics with ALMA Band 7 continuum, Band 8 [CI](1-0), and Band 3 CO(1-0) data.
key_parameters: H2 1-0 S(1) and CO(1-0) channel maps compared in velocity ranges (200, 500) km s^-1 and (500, 800) km s^-1; [CI](1-0) outflow wings integrated over (-650, -200) km s^-1 and (250, 800) km s^-1
assumptions: Thermal equilibrium for lowest rotational levels of H2.

answer_key.quantity: Rotating component flux fraction of Pa alpha

evidence.loc: Moment maps of non-rotating gas components
evidence.quote: We find that, within the NIRSpec FoV, a rotating component accounts for $35.8\pm0.4$% of the Pa$\alpha$ flux, $34.3\pm1.1$% of the H$_2$ 1-0 S(1) flux, and $35.5\pm0.5$% of the $\mathrm{[Fe\,II]\lambda 1.644\mu}$m flux (see 2).

answer_key.quantity: Rotating component flux fraction of H2 1-0 S(1)

evidence.loc: Moment maps of non-rotating gas components
evidence.quote: We find that, within the NIRSpec FoV, a rotating component accounts for $35.8\pm0.4$% of the Pa$\alpha$ flux, $34.3\pm1.1$% of the H$_2$ 1-0 S(1) flux, and $35.5\pm0.5$% of the $\mathrm{[Fe\,II]\lambda 1.644\mu}$m flux (see 2).

answer_key.quantity: Rotating component flux fraction of [Fe II] 1.644 um

evidence.loc: Moment maps of non-rotating gas components
evidence.quote: We find that, within the NIRSpec FoV, a rotating component accounts for $35.8\pm0.4$% of the Pa$\alpha$ flux, $34.3\pm1.1$% of the H$_2$ 1-0 S(1) flux, and $35.5\pm0.5$% of the $\mathrm{[Fe\,II]\lambda 1.644\mu}$m flux (see 2).

answer_key.quantity: Non-rotating (outflow) flux fraction of H2 1-0 S(1)

evidence.loc: About the H$_2$ excitation: outflow vs ISM collision?
evidence.quote: we propose that most of the H$_2$ 1-0 S(1) emission in the nuclear region of NGC 6240, as much as $66\pm2$% of its total flux (2), arises in a massive molecular outflow launched from the southern nucleus

evidence.loc: About the H$_2$ excitation: outflow vs ISM collision?
evidence.quote: measuring the H$_2$ 2-1 S(1)/H$_2$ 1-0 (S1) line ratios for all spaxels of the JWST NIRSpec map and finding that they cluster around values of 0.1-0.15, as expected for thermal emission with rotational temperature around 2000 K.
Between the AGN, approximately $1''$ south of the N AGN and slightly offset to the east, there is a compact region where the H$_2$/PAH ratio peaks ($>0.75$).

not_stated_but_needed: CASA version used for ALMA Band 7 and Band 3 data reduction and imaging
Stopping threshold / niter in tclean for Band 7 continuum and Band 3 CO(1-0) cube imaging
Image dimensions (imsize) in tclean for Band 7 and Band 3 maps
Whether primary beam correction was applied to the Band 3 CO(1-0) cube
Exact fitting wavelength window and parameter bounds for the PAH 3.3 um + H2 1-0 O(5) two-Gaussian fit
How the decision between one vs two non-rotating Gaussian components per spaxel was made (e.g., BIC/AIC or amplitude threshold)
Aperture size and exact coordinates used to extract the 'red blob' spectra of CO(1-0), [CI](1-0), and H2 1-0 S(1) in Fig. 8
missing_for_reproduction: Custom Python scripts for the pPXF + lmfit spaxel-by-spaxel decomposition and moment map generation
Exact criterion used to decide between 1 and 2 non-rotating Gaussian components per spaxel
Stopping criteria (niter/threshold) for CASA tclean imaging of ALMA Band 7 and Band 3 datasets
Interactive clean mask file for the ALMA Band 3 CO(1-0) cube
score_reason: All ALMA and JWST datasets are public, UIDs and exact frequency ranges for continuum/line-free channels are explicitly stated, and spectral fitting bounds/initial values are tabulated; minor deductions for unreleased custom fitting scripts, interactive ALMA masking, and unstated tclean stopping thresholds.
rediscovery_reason: All data are publicly available in MAST and the ALMA archive, the data reduction and pPXF/lmfit spectral decomposition recipe is well-specified with explicit parameter tables, and Table 2 provides clear quantitative flux benchmarks for total, rotating, and non-rotating line components.
